component: Persistent contextual return control (Back to ...) shown while a visit to a related area lasts, and its stacking order below modal layers

screenshots.note: The return control at the lower right of the viewport while the visit lasts, outside the navigator rail, the sheet header and the editor controls.
A modal dialog and its backdrop sit above the return control (the control is dimmed behind the backdrop).
The application drawer sits above the return control on a phone.

explanation: CaissaTrainer Phase 4 (docs/ui-migration/phase4/study-mode.md section 2.2, PuzzleStudyReturnBar.vue). OBSERVED: a person who leaves a task in one product area for a related area (a puzzle in progress, then its notebook page) needs a way back that survives navigation inside the second area. CaissaTrainer added one restrained secondary button, "Back to puzzle", fixed at the lower right of the viewport while the visit lasts (10-notes-study-1366.png) and absent in ordinary use. Findings worth keeping: (1) PLACEMENT BY MEASUREMENT: the first placement (lower left) collided with the footer of a long navigator rail, so it moved to the lower right, outside the navigator, the sheet header and the editor controls, with the page reserving 4.5rem at its end so the last line can scroll above it; below 1025px it sits above the phone context bar, never over it. (2) LAYER ORDER: it sits above the page and its sticky regions and below every drawer, scrim, toast and dialog (z-index 15 against 20 and 21 for the reading drawer, 59 to 70 for the application drawer, 1000 for toasts, 9999 and 10020 and 10050 for dialogs and sheets); a unit test reads those values from the component sources, so a later change to any layer fails instead of silently overlapping; e2e shows the dialog backdrop (12-dialog-over-control-1366.png) and the application drawer at 820 and 390 (11-drawer-over-control-390.png is attached) covering it. (3) KEYBOARD: a plain button, no key handlers, last in tab order of the page body, Escape stays with dialogs and drawers, the standard focus ring, 44px touch target. (4) HONESTY: the label and one sentence say what a press will do when it cannot fully restore ("Earlier moves were not kept. The puzzle opens again from the start and this run is not scored." and "Back to training" when a module cannot reopen one item); no fake restoration. (5) The control exists only while the visit is valid and is gone in ordinary use; browser back is a pause, only the control ends the visit. APPROVED GUIDANCE READ: P14 No Sidebar Stacking: "Secondary context: replace the sidebar content with a back chevron, or split the sidebar into upper and lower regions, or use the primary content region for details." That covers going back inside navigation structure, not a return to a task in another area. P10 Minimalism Over Prevalence (contextual and dynamic controls, one control that exists only when relevant) and P08 Familiarity (a back affordance is conventional) support the design; P18 and CHK-020 cover the 40px target. P05 supports one sentence only when the way back is not plain. No principle, anti-pattern or check speaks about a persistent return control, where it sits, or its stacking order relative to modal layers. The approved tokens have no layer scale (guidance/tokens.json and css/tokens.css define none), which is why the order had to be pinned by a test in the application. CLASSIFICATION: guidance-gap, small. Reusable by any product that sends a person from one area to a related one and expects them to come back (an order from a support ticket, a record from a report, a file from a message). Product specific, stays in CaissaTrainer: the label text ("Back to puzzle"), the module policy of what can be restored, keep-alive parking of the training page, the four hour expiry. NOTE ON FB-0042: this control is page level and is positioned against the viewport on purpose; the alignment candidate applies only to controls about a primary region, so the two do not conflict. RELATED, MERGED BY REFERENCE: FB-0024 (a modal drawer and its layering: the return control must sit below it), FB-0034 (a control must not claim what it cannot do), FB-0037 (a hidden or collapsible area must not be the only owner of a control needed to continue: the return control is the only way back, so it is always present while the visit lasts), FB-0041 (a progressive link between two product areas, see its Phase 4 update), P14.

classification.rationale: Missing reusable guideline, small. P14 covers a back chevron inside a navigation sidebar, not a persistent return to a task in another product area. P10, P08 and P18 support the design but say nothing about where such a control sits, that it must stay below drawers, dialogs and toasts, or that its label must say honestly when it cannot restore the earlier state. The approved tokens define no layer scale. Generalizes to any product that sends a person into a related area and expects them to come back. The label text, restoration policy per module and keep alive parking are product specific and stay in CaissaTrainer. Owner confirmation needed.
